question: On 11 May 2023 the Commission adopted Implementing Regulation 2023/934 laying down antidumping measures applicable to imports of high tenacity yarns of polyesters (HTYP) from China. Because the duty concerned applies only to the basic raw material, but not to finished products made from it, there are adverse economic consequences for firms that produce in Europe. Indeed, there are firms that make HTYP-only finished products, such as slings. 1.
Has the Commission given sufficient consideration to the fact that there are firms in the EU that make HTYP-only finished products?

Why did the Commission opt for an anti-dumping duty on only the basic raw material, HTYP, but not on finished products derived from it, while China grants an export subsidy for both the basic raw material and finished products?

Is the Commission prepared to open an investigation into the dumping of HTYP final products from China, for example by creating an HS code for products that are at least 98% composed of the same raw material as HTYP (5402 0000) and carrying out an appraisal of that specific HS code?
answer: In anti-dumping and anti-subsidy investigations, the Commission is obliged to conduct a EU- interest test to examine whether the imposition or continued imposition of measures would be against the interests of the EU, as a whole.

In the expiry review on measures on high tenacity yarns of polyesters (HTYP) from China, the Commission performed the obligatory EU- interest test which assessed the impact on users of the product. Recitals 216-252 of the Implementing Regulation (1) set out the analysis and findings where it was concluded that there were no compelling reasons against the maintenance of the measures in this case.

The measures were limited to the product HTYP as the Commission acts on the basis of substantiated complaints received from industry, which, in this case, concerned HTYP and not finished products made from that material. The Commission refers to Recital 239 of the Implementing Regulation (2) where this issue is discussed in detail.

The Commission is committed to protecting the EU industry from unfair and injurious trading practices by robustly using the trade defence instruments at its disposal. The Commission stands ready to open an investigation regarding imports of any product, if it were to receive a complaint from industry which fulfils all the evidentiary requirements of the basic anti-dumping Regulation (3).
